title: boundary_check excluded findings/ from the public-surface scan, so an adopter name committed in an engine ticket leaked to the public repo undetected
detail: getprusik/prusik is PUBLIC and the engine's own findings/*.json tickets are committed there, but boundary_check's PUBLIC_SURFACE list excluded findings/ as 'private plane' — a correct assumption for an ADOPTER's private repo, wrong for the public engine. Two engine tickets carried an adopter name in their detail ('<adopter> walkthrough 2026-07-27: …') and rode to the public remote for weeks, undetected by the identity gate. Fix: add findings/ to PUBLIC_SURFACE so committed tickets are scanned; the id→adopter crosswalk stays in the private plane (prusik-hq / the adopter's repo), the public engine's findings cite by fb-<id> only. HEAD scrubbed to generic 'Adopter walkthrough'. Residual: the names remain in git HISTORY on the public remote (already public since v0.197.35) — a separate operator decision on whether to rewrite public history.

resolution.verify: CUR=$(prusik --version 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$CUR" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' '0.212.0' "$CUR" | sort -V | head -1)" = '0.212.0' ] && echo "1 passed: engine carries moat-proven fix fb-ac17c362d5c6 (prusik $CUR >= 0.212.0)"
